With the restricted solution fields these are developments of the complete data on $S$. This is Theorems 3.6 and 3.13 of Sbierski's paper. The patching step 4.1 is the place where the source writes "the same continuity argument as in the proof of Lemma 3.1, applied to $N\cap U$": it is made precise here through the limiting first jet at the base point $s\in S$ of the radial segment, using clause (c)3 of [[lem-gr-spacelike-restart-hypersurface]] instead of a density argument. Step 1.1 treats the two sides separately. The full past-side geometric construction is [[lem-gr-past-corresponding-boundary-restart]], with future radial flow and its signed future-endpoint argument. The local uniqueness invocation in step 2.1 uses the actual complete data on $S$ with the original future unit normal in both branches. Neither $N$, the initial $K$, nor any scalar, fluid, dust or additional model field is reversed; no invariance of a fixed model under time reversal is assumed.

Countable Choice supplies the countable atlas and smooth partition. Dependent Choice is inherited from the actual maximal-common and no-corresponding-boundary supplier theorems; no arbitrary-index Axiom of Choice is used.

5.1 (Metric, full matter and a future orientation field.) The pushed metrics and each fixed-model matter tensor agree on the overlap because $p_{M'}\circ\varphi=p_M$ and $\varphi$ preserves them. Thus they define smooth $\bar g,\bar\psi$ on $Q$. Future cones also agree, since the common map preserves the time orientation as a cone. The representing fields $N,N'$ themselves need not agree there. By steps 4.2-4.3, $Q$ is a Hausdorff second countable smooth manifold. Under Countable Choice, a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_M,\rho_{M'})$ for its two-member open cover exists by [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]. Define $\bar N=\rho_M(p_M)_*N+\rho_{M'}(p_{M'})_*N'$, extending each supported term by zero. This is smooth, and at each point is a nonzero future timelike vector because the weights sum to one and the timelike cone is convex ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]). Both member maps therefore preserve the future cones of $\bar N$. All field equations depend on the metric and full fixed-model matter, rather than the arbitrary orientation representative. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, step 4.3, L2, algebra, construct]

6.1 (The field equations and the induced data.) The equations of the data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)4) are local and hold on $M$ and $M'$, so they hold on $Q$ because $Q$ is covered by the images of the two isometries (step 5.1). The map $\bar j=\pi\circ\iota_M\circ j=p_M\circ j:\Sigma\to Q$ is an embedding with spacelike image, since $p_M$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open set and $j$ has these properties in $M$; its induced metric, second fundamental form and matter data are $(h,K,\psi_0)$ because $p_M$ is a data-fixing isometry ([L2]). [step 5.1, L2, algebra]

8.1 (Conclusion.) The preceding steps exhibit $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ as a time-oriented second countable smooth Lorentzian four-manifold satisfying the field equations on $Q$, with $\bar j(\Sigma)$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface meeting every inextendible causal curve exactly once and carrying the induced data of the same initial data: a development of the data. The maps $p_M:M\to Q$ and $p_{M'}:M'\to Q$ are diffeomorphisms onto open subsets, isometric, time-orientation preserving, matter preserving and satisfy $p_M\circ j=\bar j=p_{M'}\circ j'$ (step 3.1), so they are data-fixing development embeddings. This proves (a), (b) and (c). [step 4.1, step 4.3, step 6.1, step 7.1, algebra] ∎

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix the data of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$,
one fixed admissible covariant matter model with its complete smooth Cauchy
data $d$, and constants $\Lambda,\kappa$. The model and its complete data,
including all required initial derivatives and prescribed fields on empty
regions, are fixed throughout. Assume the supplied complete-data local
existence and geometric uniqueness hypotheses apply on every spacelike
restart surface occurring in comparisons, as required by that definition.
Assume that at least one development of these data exists.
Write $Z_0:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ and let $j_0:\Sigma\to Z_0$,
$j_0(x):=(x,0)$.

[L2] Maximal common developments and pair gluing: for any two members $\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal X$ their maximal common development $(U_{\alpha\beta},\varphi_{\alpha\beta})$ exists, is a common subdevelopment realised inside $U_\alpha$, and contains the image of $\Sigma$; the pair quotient $Q_{\alpha\beta}:=(U_\alpha\sqcup U_\beta)/{\sim_{\alpha\beta}}$ of [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] is a development of the data which is Hausdorff, second countable and smooth, in which $U_\alpha$ and $U_\beta$ embed by data-fixing development embeddings; the maximality property of [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] clause (b) applies to every common subdevelopment ([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]], [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] clauses (a)-(c)).

4.1 (The local smooth structure, fields and future cones.) Compose the charts of each member with $(\pi|_{U_\alpha})^{-1}$. On $Q_\alpha\cap Q_\beta=\pi(U_{\alpha\beta})$, the transitions use the smooth data-fixing diffeomorphism $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$, so these charts generate a unique maximal compatible smooth atlas. The metrics and matter fields agree on overlaps and descend to $\bar g,\bar\psi$; the field equations hold locally. The pushforwards of $N_\alpha$ need not agree as vectors, but they select the same future timelike component on every overlap because $\varphi_{\alpha\beta}$ preserves future cones. Thus there is a consistent locally smooth choice of future cones, before any global representative field is asserted. The maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}\circ j_0$ agree and define an embedded spacelike $S:=\bar j(\Sigma)$ with the prescribed induced data, since every member contains this entire surface and each member map is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset. [step 3.1, L2, algebra]

10.1 (Universality.) For an arbitrary development $M$, use its canonical representative $D:=\Sigma\times\mathbb R\in\mathcal X$ and diffeomorphism $\chi:D\to M$ from step 1.2. The map $(\pi|_D)\circ\chi^{-1}:M\to Q$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset, an isometry preserving future cones and matter fields, and takes $j$ to $\bar j$. Hence it is a data-fixing development embedding, proving (e). [step 1.2, step 7.1, step 9.1, algebra]

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:
**Given:** the universal development $Q$ of [[lem-gr-universal-development]] with its covering family of member maps, and the initial surface $\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$.

[L1] Structural properties of $Q$: every $Q_\alpha$ is open, the maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ are diffeomorphisms onto the $Q_\alpha$, and $Q$ carries a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$ with respect to which each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$ is an isometry; $Q$ is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean ([[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d)). Each member $U_\alpha$ is a development of the data, hence globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_0(\Sigma)$ by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]] ([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c), [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)).

[L4] Timelike chords in convex balls: if $x\ll z$ are two points of a strictly convex normal ball $B$ and $z$ lies on the endpoint set in $B$ of a future timelike curve with image in $B$ starting at $x$, then $z=\exp_x(w)$ for a timelike $w$ ([[lem-gr-convex-normal-causality]] clause (a), applied with base point $x$). The set of timelike vectors at a point is open in the tangent space, and the rational span of a basis is dense in the tangent space in the coordinates of that basis ([[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]], [[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]).

1.2 (Chains of timelike chords, including the past direction.) Fix $p\in Q$ and a member $Q_\alpha$ containing it. In that member the complete flow of [L5] joins a point $z_0\in S:=\bar j(\Sigma)$ to $p$ with a parameter $t_1\in\mathbb R$. If $t_1=0$, then $p\in S$ and is already in the closure of $D_0$. Otherwise finitely many convex normal neighborhoods cover this compact flow segment; a sufficiently fine finite partition of the segment has each subsegment contained in one of those neighborhoods. Write the ordered endpoints along the flow from $S$ to $p$ as $z_0,\ldots,z_k=p$. The inverse velocity $w_i=v(z_{i-1},z_i)$ for each contained joining geodesic is timelike by [L4], using future chords when $t_1>0$ and past chords when $t_1<0$ (reverse the future-directed chord and use the time reversal of the geodesic). The recursion includes both future and past timelike vectors. [L1, L3, L4, L5, construct]

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ and the member maps
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as in
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d): $Q$ is a Hausdorff locally
Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, the
open sets $Q_\alpha$ cover $Q$, and each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$
is a diffeomorphism onto $Q_\alpha$. Let $D\subseteq Q$ be a countable dense
subset, as supplied by [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]]. When
$Q$ and $D$ are obtained from these development suppliers, retain their
Countable Choice and Dependent Choice hypotheses ([[def-dependent-choice]]).
The basis construction conditional on the supplied $Q,D$ uses Countable
Choice only. Choose one
basis at each $d\in D$. In these coordinates let
$B_d(a,r)\subseteq T_dQ$ be the Euclidean open ball centered at
$a\in\mathbb Q^4$ with radius $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, and let
$\mathcal E_d$ be the maximal exponential domain. Then
$$\mathcal B:=\{\exp_d(B_d(a,r)):d\in D, a\in\mathbb Q^4, r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}, B_d(a,r)\subseteq\mathcal E_d, \exp_d|_{B_d(a,r)}\text{ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of }Q\}$$
is a countable basis of the topology of $Q$. This exhibits an explicit basis
for the second-countability conclusion of
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clause (d).

[L1] The member images are open and cover $Q$, and the member maps are diffeomorphisms preserving the metric ([[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d)). Exponential maps agree with their member counterparts whenever the corresponding segment stays in the member, by uniqueness of the geodesic ODE ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]).

Translated balls are necessary in this construction: after one selects arbitrarily small normal domains at dense centers, their centered subballs need not cover any prescribed point outside $D$. The family above uses all rational translated balls on which the exponential is a diffeomorphism, rather than one selected normal domain per center. The proof gives a general local-exponential countability criterion and does not invoke the conclusion of second countability from the universal-development lemma.

Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$,
$\kappa>0$, let $\Sigma$ be a connected smooth three-manifold with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$ and smooth symmetric $2$-tensor $K$, and let smooth
complete matter initial data be given for one fixed admissible covariant coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]], with the constraints satisfied and at least one development existing. The supplied local existence and uniqueness obligations must hold for that same model and for the complete data at every spacelike restart used in the proof. This includes vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic nonnegative tilted dust (with velocity prescribed through zero density) via [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]; additional fixed models must supply the same actual obligations. Then there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of the data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]
clause (a) that is maximal in the sense of clause (d) of that definition:
for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the same data there is a
data-fixing development embedding $M\to M_{\mathrm{max}}$. Moreover, if
$(M'_{\mathrm{max}},g'_{\mathrm{max}},N'_{\mathrm{max}},j'_{\mathrm{max}},\psi'_{\mathrm{max}})$
is another maximal development of the same data, then there is exactly one
data-fixing isometry $M_{\mathrm{max}}\to M'_{\mathrm{max}}$; the maximal
development is thus unique up to a unique data-fixing isometry. It is
connected and, by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]],
globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface $j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$.

**Given:** Countable Choice, Dependent Choice, connected complete constrained initial data of the specified fixed admissible model, and at least one development, with the actual branch local existence and geometric uniqueness/restart obligations supplied.

[L1] The set-sized family and the quotient: the family $\mathcal X$ of canonical developments over $\Sigma\times\mathbb R$ is a set, the generated identification relation on the disjoint union is given by the pairwise maximal common developments, and the quotient $Q$ is Hausdorff, locally Euclidean and smooth with a Lorentzian metric, time orientation and matter fields, all member maps being diffeomorphisms onto open sets preserving the structure; these maps are data-fixing isometries onto their images, and every causal curve in $Q$ inextendible in $Q$ meets the initial surface exactly once ([[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (a)-(d)).
[L3] Every development embeds into $Q$: for every development $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ of the data there is a data-fixing development embedding into $Q$ ([[lem-gr-universal-development]] clause (e)).

1.1 (Existence.) Let $Q$ be the quotient of [[lem-gr-universal-development]]. By [L1] it is Hausdorff and locally Euclidean with a smooth atlas, metric, time orientation and matter fields; by [L2] it is second countable; by [L1] its initial surface is met exactly once by every inextendible causal curve and the field equations and induced data hold. Hence by [L6] $Q$ is a development of the data. [L1, L2, L6, algebra]

4.1 (Conclusion.) The preceding steps show that the quotient $Q$ of [[lem-gr-universal-development]] is a maximal development of the data to which every development embeds by a data-fixing development embedding, and that any two maximal developments are related by exactly one data-fixing isometry. This is the assertion. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

The theorem is the mathematical content of Sbierski's Theorems 2.7 and 2.8 for the stated fixed admissible coupled model, including the four concrete smooth matter branches. The physical reading of the objects, and the question whether the data represent an observed configuration, are not part of this statement; see [[pthm-gr-smooth-maximal-development]] for the conditional model deduction and [[rem-gr-mghd-scope]] for the empirical qualifications. For disconnected second countable initial data the proof is applied to the at most countably many connected components and their disjoint union, which is again second countable; every development restricts componentwise by its Cauchy surface, so the same existence, maximality and uniqueness statements hold.

Riemannian metric and $K$ a smooth symmetric $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$, and let
complete smooth initial data for one fixed admissible coupled model of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] be given, satisfying the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]. Assume its actual local existence and uniqueness/restart hypotheses, including complete matter initialization and recovery. The concrete branches of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] include vacuum, scalar, strict fluid and nonnegative tilted geodesic dust with velocity through zero density; any further model must supply the same fixed-model obligations. Then, as a conditional deduction from the
adopted model:

**(a)** there exists a development
$(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}},N_{\mathrm{max}},j_{\mathrm{max}},\psi_{\mathrm{max}})$
of these data in which $g_{\mathrm{max}}$ solves the adopted field law with
the adopted stress-energy tensor and the matter fields solve the adopted
matter equations, and which is maximal among developments of the same data
in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (d);

**(c)** $M_{\mathrm{max}}$ is globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface
$j_{\mathrm{max}}(\Sigma)$, so the deduction yields a deterministic
initial-value formulation inside the model for those complete constrained data that also satisfy the stated admissibility and local/restart hypotheses.

**Given:** Countable Choice, Dependent Choice, the adopted postulates [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]], [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], and complete initial data of the fixed admissible model satisfying the constraints and actual local/restart hypotheses.

[F2] Matter assumptions: the specified fixed model's full field content, equations and stress expression are adopted as premises. The concrete vacuum, scalar, strict barotropic fluid and geodesic nonnegative tilted dust branches have the explicit definitions and regularity/recovery requirements in [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] ([[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]], [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]).

Use [[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]] only when its full harmonic initialization, compatibility recovery, admissibility and conservation hypotheses hold; geodesic nonnegative tilted dust uses its independent common-flow/frame branch, including the prescribed velocity through zero density, in [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]]. The same model hypotheses must apply to each realized spacelike restart.

[A1] Scope: the constraint equations are conditions on $(h,K)$ and the matter initial data in the model; they are not empirical observations, and the data are model inputs ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]], [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). No statistical, measurement or apparatus assumptions enter this deduction.

1.1 (Relating the postulates to the mathematical model.) By [F1] and [F2] the field law and matter equations are those of the specified fixed model, with its complete data and actual admissibility/local uniqueness obligations; the four concrete sectors of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] are included at their stated branch hypotheses. By [A1] the constraint equations are the model's compatibility conditions on the data. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

This item records the model-level content of the mathematical theorem [[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]]: postulating the field law and matter models, constraint-satisfying smooth data determine a maximal globally hyperbolic development uniquely up to isometry fixing the data. The physical interpretation of $(M_{\mathrm{max}},g_{\mathrm{max}})$, the status of the idealisation of smoothness and of the specific matter sectors, the absence of any claim of global existence, completeness or genericity, and the boundary between model deduction and observation are recorded in [[rem-gr-mghd-scope]]. actual_use_passages:
**(b)** the glued quotient of [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] is
isometric, in a data-fixing way, to Minkowski spacetime itself, the two
embeddings being the identity and the inverse translation.

[L2] Common subdevelopments and the maximal common development: $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$ ([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)), the maximal one exists and contains every common subdevelopment with the same map ([[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] clauses (a)-(b)), and the pair quotient of [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] is a development of the data in which both members embed by data-fixing development embeddings.

## Verification
1.1 ($\psi$ is a data-fixing isometry.) The translation $\psi$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ preserving $\eta$, the time orientation and (vacuously) the matter fields, and $\psi\circ j=j'$ by definition of $j,j'$. Hence $\psi:M\to M'$ is a development embedding of the whole of $M$, and $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)). [given, L1, algebra]

2.1 (Maximality.) By [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] the maximal common development $(U^*,\psi^*)$ contains every common subdevelopment, so $U^*=M$ and $\psi^*=\psi$ by step 1.1 applied to $(U^*,\psi^*)$ in the reverse direction. In particular $U$ has no boundary in $M$, hence no corresponding boundary points, in accordance with [[lem-gr-no-corresponding-boundary-points]]. This is (a). [step 1.1, L2, algebra]

3.1 (The quotient.) By [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] the quotient $Q:=(M\sqcup M')/{\sim}$ with the identifications along $\psi$ is a development of the data and the maps $p_M,p_{M'}$ are data-fixing development embeddings; here every point of $M$ is identified with its image in $M'$ and conversely, so the canonical map $M\to Q$, $p\mapsto[p]$, is a bijection and an isometry: its inverse is the map sending the class of $m\in M$ to $m$ and the class of $m'\in M'$ to $\psi^{-1}(m')$, which is well defined because $m'\sim\psi^{-1}(m')$ and because $\psi$ is a bijection. Both compositions with $\eta$ agree, so $Q$ is isometric to $M$ by a data-fixing isometry; the two development embeddings are the identity and the inverse translation. This is (b). [step 2.1, L2, algebra] ∎

actual_use_passages: [L1] The dense-set recursion of [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]] with initial set $j(\Sigma)$ and datum $D_0=S_0$ produces the countable set $D$ of that lemma.

[L2] The exponential family of rational balls is a countable basis of $Q$ ([[lem-gr-development-quotient-second-countable]]); the exponential map of Minkowski spacetime in standard coordinates is $v\mapsto d+v$ along straight geodesics ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]] clause (a)).

2.1 (Countability and density.) $D$ is countable by the construction ([[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]], [[def-countable]]) and contains $\mathbb Q^4$, which is dense in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ by the density of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb R$ coordinatewise ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]); hence $D$ is dense and meets $j(\Sigma)=\{t=0\}$ in $\{0\}\times\mathbb Q^3$. [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

3.1 (The basis.) The repaired abstract family uses translated rational tangent balls: here $\exp_d(B(a,r))=B(d+a,r)$. Since $d,a$ are rational, its centers are rational; conversely every rational center is obtained by taking $a=0$ and that center as $d$. Thus it is exactly the Euclidean rational-center family declared above.  For $d\in D$ and rational $r>0$ the set $\exp_d(B(0;r))=d+B(0;r)$ is the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ around $d$ centred at a rational point with rational radius; the family of all such balls is a countable basis of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-topology-basis-subbasis]], [[def-second-countable-space]]). In particular $\mathcal B$ as defined in the statement is a countable basis of the topology of $M$, so $M$ is second countable, in accordance with [[lem-gr-development-quotient-second-countable]]. [step 2.1, L2, algebra] ∎
